summary_of_change:
Fortinet's actual sequential operating performance reflects strong momentum at the surface, driven by an aggressive hardware product refresh cycle. In the latest quarter (Q2 2026), revenue expanded 25.6% year-over-year to $2,047.9M, establishing an annualized run-rate of $8,191.6M, while total billings accelerated 33.0% YoY to $2,370M. Product revenue was the standout engine, surging 51.8% YoY to $773.0M as enterprise clients upgraded legacy Gen-6 appliances to secure AI boundary connectivity, high-throughput OT perimeter operations, and multi-gigabit campus architectures. Non-GAAP gross margin remained resilient at 80.9%, and GAAP operating margin expanded to 34.0% (38.0% Non-GAAP), demonstrating the operating leverage inherent in Fortinet's proprietary custom ASIC silicon.

Operationally, Fortinet retains dominant unit distribution, shipping more physical units than Palo Alto Networks, Check Point, and Cisco combined, with global firewall unit shipment market share holding firmly above 50% to 55%. The company's architectural moat—anchored by custom FortiASIC processors (such as the SP6 co-designed with Intel) and the unified FortiOS 8.0 code base—delivers a 50% to 70% total cost of ownership discount compared to off-the-shelf x86 CPU firewalls. Dedicated FortiSASE billings expanded over 100% YoY, and Operational Technology security grew over 55% YoY, validating that the platform's reach extends beyond traditional on-premise appliances.

Cash flow generation and capital discipline remain robust. Trailing cash flow from operations reached $1,040M in the most recent quarter, supported by positive working capital float from upfront multi-year subscription contracts. Management repurchased $146M of common stock in Q2 2026 under its expanded buyback program, keeping share count tightly controlled at 739.9M diluted shares and closing the period with $3,573M in liquid net cash ($+4.83 per share).
